items.title: Example of Lamarckism: Evolution of giraffe neck

source_refs.note: Example of Lamarckism: Evolution of giraffe neck: a main subheading of Lamarck's Theory and the Giraffe, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 224-224.

blocks.text: The evolution of a giraffe's neck is often used as the example to prove Lamarckism. The ancestors of giraffe did not have long necks. They used to eat grass or the leaves of small plants. Changes occurred in the environment and small plants were no more available to them. In the new situation, some individuals of the population began stretching their necks to reach the leaves of tall trees as alternative. When they constantly did so, their necks became strong and long during their lifetime. This was an acquired character. When these individuals reproduced, this acquired characters was inherited to their next generation i.e., new individuals were born with slightly longer necks. When these individuals grew up, they continued the same practice of stretching their necks. In this way, their necks became even more stronger and longer. This gave rise to an acquired character. When this acquired character was inherited to many generations, the generation with long necks evolved.

blocks.alt: Four giraffes in three shaded zones with leafy branches above. Short-necked ancestor: a short-necked giraffe below a branch it cannot reach. Necks became long as a result of stretching: a giraffe with a longer neck stretching to the leaves. Acquired characters passed to next generations: two giraffes with still longer necks reaching higher branches. Red arrows lead from each giraffe to the next.
